example.ring: A=k[ε]/(ε²), for a fixed field k; S=Spec A.
example.schemes: X1=Y1=Spec k and X2=Y2=Spec A, all with their indicated A-structures.
example.morphisms: f1=id_Spec k and f2=id_Spec A. These are S-morphisms locally of finite type.
example.products: X=X1×_SX2=Spec(k⊗_A A)=Spec k and Y=Y1×_SY2=Spec k. Under these canonical ring identifications f=f1×_Sf2 is id_Spec k.
example.tor_independence: For both pairs (X1,X2) and (Y1,Y2), the relevant higher Tor modules are Tor_i^A(k,A)=0, since A is free of rank one over itself. These are exactly the two pairs printed in III4.7.
example.inputs: E1=k[0] on X1 and E2=k[0] on X2. E1 has perfect amplitude [0,0] relative to the identity f1. E2 has bounded cohomology in degree0 and is pseudo-coherent relative to the identity f2.
example.pseudo_coherence_proof: Let P^n=A for n≤0, P^n=0 for n>0, and d^n=ε for n<0. The augmentation P^0=A→k is the quotient. Because ε²=0 and ker(A --ε→ A)=εA=im(A --ε→ A), H^n(P)=0 for n<0 and H^0(P)=k. Thus P→k[0] is a free resolution. Every term has rank one; truncating sufficiently far to the left gives a finite-free approximation in any prescribed upper range, proving pseudo-coherence of k[0].

exact_derived_tensor_calculation: On X=Spec k, pr1:X→X1 is the identity and pr2:X→X2 corresponds to A→k. Hence Lpr1^*E1 is k[0], and Lpr2^*E2 is k⊗^L_A k.

The definition in III1.6 gives E1⊗^L_S E2=(Lpr1^*E1)⊗^L_{O_X}(Lpr2^*E2). The unit isomorphism k⊗^L_k(−)→(−) identifies it with k⊗^L_A k. Using the explicit free resolution P, this is represented by k⊗_A P.
Multiplication by ε becomes zero after tensoring with k. Thus k⊗_A P has term k in every degree n≤0 and zero differential. It follows directly that H^n(k⊗^L_A k)=k for every n≤0.

The output is a bounded-above pseudo-coherent complex over k, but it has no lower cohomology bound. For the exact inclusion J:D^b(k)_coh→D^−(k)_coh, every object in its essential image has a lower cohomology bound. Cohomology is invariant under derived isomorphism, so this explicit output cannot be isomorphic to J(B) for any B in D^b(k)_coh.

Consequently the first displayed tensor functor does not have the asserted bounded target for these inputs. The first Grothendieck map is not supplied by that advertised functor. This conclusion concerns the specific tensor construction, and makes no claim that no abstract bilinear map between the underlying groups can exist.
relation_to_the_projection_domain_decisi: The separate correction in identification_295.json concerns 3.3.2.3. Its second branch uses E perfect relative to X→S itself, so E has finite S-amplitude. In the present example E1 is perfect relative to id_Spec k, while its S-amplitude is unbounded: the same Tor computation gives Tor_i^A(k,k)=k in every degree. The identity of the underlying complex does not identify these two relative-amplitude conditions. The explicit structural map Spec k→Spec A and its derived pullback compute their relationship.
